UserAnalyticsQueryFilters.description: The data a query runs on. The tenant (organization) is not a filter: it always comes from the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header

from.description: The start of the time range (inclusive): `now`, `now-<n><unit>` with a unit among `s`, `m`, `h` and `d` (like `now-30m` or `now-7d`), or an ISO-8601 instant (like `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`). `now-1h` when missing or invalid

to.description: The end of the time range (exclusive): `now`, `now-<n><unit>` with a unit among `s`, `m`, `h` and `d` (like `now-30m` or `now-7d`), or an ISO-8601 instant (like `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`). `now` when missing or invalid

route_id.description: Only keep the requests handled by this route (its id)

api_id.description: Only keep the requests handled by this api (its id)

apikey_id.description: Only keep the requests made with this api key (its client id)

group_id.description: Only keep the requests handled by a route of this service group (its id)

err.description: Only keep the requests in error (`true`) or the successful ones (`false`)

UserAnalyticsQueryRequest.description: The body of `POST /api/analytics/_query`: the id of a query of the catalog, its parameters, the data it runs on, the size of its time buckets and how its result is cached

query.description: The id of the query, as listed by `GET /api/analytics/_schema`

params.description: The parameters of the query, as listed in its `params`, like `{"top_n": 10}` for the top N queries

filters.description: The data the query runs on: the last hour of every request of the tenant (organization) when absent

bucket.description: The time bucket size of timeseries and heatmaps: `1m`, `5m`, `1h`, `6h` or `1d`. When missing or unknown, it depends on the time range: up to 1 hour `1m`, up to 24 hours `1h`, up to 7 days `6h`, `1d` beyond

compare.description: Also run the query on the previous period of the same length and return it in `compare`. Ignored by the queries that do not support it (`supports_compare` in the catalog)

nocache.description: Run the query even if its result is in the cache, and do not cache the new one

UserAnalyticsQueryData.description: The result of a query. Its fields depend on `shape`: `scalar` has `value` and `label`, `pie` has `label` and `items` (with `key` and `value`), `topN` has `items` (with `key`, `label` and `value`), `timeseries` has `bucket` and either `points` (one series) or `series` (several named series), `heatmap` has `bucket`, `xBuckets`, `yBuckets` and `values`. The layout of `metric` and `table` results, and of the results of the queries of admin extensions, is up to the extension providing the query

label.description: The label of a `scalar` or `pie` result

items.description: The items of a `pie` or `topN` result, biggest first

bucket.description: The time bucket size of a `timeseries` or `heatmap` result

points.description: The points of a single series `timeseries` result, one per bucket

series.description: The series of a multi-series `timeseries` result

xBuckets.description: The time buckets of a `heatmap` result (X axis), as unix timestamps in milliseconds

yBuckets.description: The response time ranges of a `heatmap` result (Y axis), from `<50ms` to `>=3s`

values.description: The request counts of a `heatmap` result, one row per `yBuckets` entry and one column per `xBuckets` entry

UserAnalyticsQueryItem.description: An item of a `pie` or `topN` result

key.description: What is counted: a status code, a method, a route id, an api key client id, ... `(unknown)` when the events do not hold it

label.description: A readable name for `key` (the route name for routes, `key` otherwise). `topN` only

value.description: The number of requests counted for `key` on the time range, only the failed ones for `top_error_routes`

UserAnalyticsTimeseriesPoint.description: A point of a timeseries: the value of a time bucket. Every bucket of the time range has its point, the buckets without data included

ts.description: The start of the time bucket, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds

value.description: The value for this time bucket (0 when there is no data)

UserAnalyticsTimeseriesSeries.description: A named series of a multi-series timeseries

name.description: The name of the series, like `p95`, `data_in` or `5xx`

points.description: The points of the series, one per bucket

UserAnalyticsQueryResult.description: The result of a user analytics query on a period

shape.description: The shape of the result, which tells the fields of `data` (see `UserAnalyticsQueryData`) and the widget types that can draw it

raw.description: The rows behind `data`, when the query provides them. Empty for multi-series timeseries and heatmaps

items.description: A row: an item of a `pie` or `topN` result, a point of a timeseries, the `value` of a `scalar` result

meta.description: Execution details, merged into the details the query adds itself (none for the built-in queries). In `compare`, only the details the query adds

execution_ms.description: The time it took to run the query, in milliseconds. Missing when the result comes from the cache

from_cache.description: Whether the result, and its comparison when there is one, comes from the 30 seconds result cache

bucket.description: The time bucket size used by the query

UserAnalyticsQueryResponse.description: The result of a user analytics query, with its comparison with the previous period when asked for

compare.description: The result of the same query on the previous period of the same length. Only present when `compare` was asked for and the query supports it

UserAnalyticsQueryCatalog.description: The catalog of the user analytics queries, the ones of the admin extensions included, and the widget types of the dashboards

queries.description: The queries a query request, a dashboard widget or an alert condition can run, the built-in ones first

widget_types.description: The values the `type` of a dashboard widget can take

UserAnalyticsQueryDefinition.description: A query of the catalog: its id, what it computes, the shape of its result, its parameters and whether it can be compared with the previous period

id.description: The id to use in `POST /api/analytics/_query` and in dashboard widgets

name.description: The readable name of the query, the default title of the widgets the backoffice creates on it

shape.description: The shape of the result of the query, which tells the fields of its `data`

default_widget.description: The widget type that displays the query by default, one of the `widget_types` of the catalog for the built-in queries

params.description: The parameters the query reads in the `params` of a query request, a widget or an alert condition. Empty when it takes none

supports_compare.description: Whether the query can be compared with the previous period: `compare` is ignored when it cannot

UserAnalyticsQueryParam.description: A parameter of a user analytics query

name.description: The name of the parameter in `params`

kind.description: The type of the parameter, like `int`

default.description: The value used when the parameter is missing, `null` when there is none

UserAnalyticsProjection.description: A family of events the user-analytics data exporter can store, each one in its own table: the gateway events, the fired user alerts, and the families of the admin extensions

id.description: The id of the projection, to use in `excluded_projections`

name.description: The readable name of the projection, shown in the settings of the user-analytics data exporter where projections can be excluded

description.description: What the events of the projection are and what stops working without them, shown next to its name
description.example: Every request proxied by Otoroshi. Feeds the core queries, the default dashboards and most alerts.

core.description: Whether the projection is built into otoroshi (`false` when an admin extension provides it)

table.description: The table the events are written to, with its schema, computed from the `schema` and `table_prefix` query parameters. `null` when the projection cannot tell

example.name: Gateway events
example.description: Every request proxied by Otoroshi. Feeds the core queries, the default dashboards and most alerts.

UserAnalyticsExporterSettings.description: The settings of a user-analytics data exporter (its `config`): the PostgreSQL database the exporter writes the events to, where the user analytics queries, dashboards and alerts read them

uri.description: A PostgreSQL connection uri, like `postgresql://user:password@host:5432/database`. Used instead of the other connection settings when present and not empty

host.description: The host name or ip address of the PostgreSQL server. Ignored when `uri` is set

port.description: The port of the PostgreSQL server. Ignored when `uri` is set

database.description: The PostgreSQL database that holds the tables. Ignored when `uri` is set

user.description: The PostgreSQL user otoroshi connects as. It must be allowed to create the schema, the tables and the indexes, which the exporter does when it starts. Ignored when `uri` is set

password.description: The password of `user`. Ignored when `uri` is set

schema.description: The PostgreSQL schema of the tables, created when it does not exist

table_prefix.description: The name of the table of the gateway events, and the prefix of the names of the other tables (`<table_prefix>_fired_alerts`, the tables of the projections of the admin extensions). `table` is read instead when it is absent or empty

table.description: The former name of `table_prefix`, always written with its value for the nodes that predate the rename. Only read when `table_prefix` is absent or empty, as in the configs saved before the rename

pool_size.description: The maximum number of connections the exporter opens to the database

ssl.description: Whether the connection to the database requires tls (`sslmode=require`). Ignored when `uri` is set: the uri tells it

retention_days.description: How long the events of every projection are kept, in days: an hourly job deletes the older ones from the tables of the active user-analytics data exporter. `0` (or less) keeps them forever

statement_timeout_ms.description: The maximum duration of a query, in milliseconds. Reserved: it is not applied yet

rollup_enabled.description: Reserved: rollup tables are not computed yet

excluded_projections.description: The ids of the projections whose events are not stored (see `GET /api/analytics/_projections`). Their tables are still created and pruned, and their queries keep answering with the events stored before

UserAnalyticsOkResponse.description: The outcome of an operation on a user analytics database

UserAnalyticsSetActiveExporterResponse.description: The outcome of the activation of a user-analytics data exporter

ok.description: Always `true`: the exporter is now the active one

active.description: The id of the data exporter that is now the active user-analytics data exporter, the `id` of the path

demoted_count.description: The number of the other exporters that were flagged as active before

seeded_default.description: The `otoroshi-default-id` metadata of the default dashboards that were missing and are now created

UserAnalyticsRestoreDefaultsResponse.description: The default dashboards that were missing and are now created

created.description: The default ids of the dashboards that were created (kept in their `otoroshi-default-id` metadata)

count.description: The number of dashboards that were created

UserAnalyticsAlertEventsPage.description: A page of fired events of a user alert

limit.description: The maximum number of events of the page, the `limit` query parameter brought back between 1 and 2000 (200 by default)

offset.description: The number of events skipped before the page, the `offset` query parameter (0 by default)

items.message: More than 5% of the requests failed

UserAnalyticsAlertEvent.description: A fired event of a user alert, as stored in the `<table_prefix>_fired_alerts` table of the active user-analytics data exporter, with the evaluation of its conditions and its acknowledgement

id.description: The id of the fired event (the `@id` of the alert event, a snowflake id), to use in the paths that acknowledge it

ts.description: When the alert fired, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds

tenant.description: The tenant (organization) of the user alert: only the events of the tenant of the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header are answered

alert_id.description: The id of the user alert that fired, the `alertId` of the path

alert_name.description: The name of the user alert when it fired

severity.description: The severity of the user alert, like `info`, `warning` or `critical`

message.description: The `message` of the user alert when it fired
message.example: More than 5% of the requests failed

combine.description: How the conditions were combined: `AND` or `OR`

windowSeconds.description: The time window the conditions were evaluated on, in seconds

conditions.description: The evaluation of each condition of the alert

seen_at.description: When the event was acknowledged, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds

seen_by.description: The email of the admin who acknowledged the event, `?` when it was acknowledged through the admin api without a backoffice user

example.message: More than 5% of the requests failed

UserAnalyticsAlertConditionEval.description: How a condition of a user alert was evaluated when the alert fired: the reduced result of its query, compared to its threshold

query.description: The id of the query of the condition

reducer.description: How the query result was reduced to a single value: `avg`, `max`, `min`, `sum` or `last`

operator.description: How the value was compared to the threshold: `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `==` or `!=`

threshold.description: The value the reduced value was compared to, the `threshold` of the condition

value.description: The result of the query reduced to a single number, `null` when the query answered no value or could not run

error.description: Why the condition could not be evaluated (no active user-analytics data exporter, an unknown query, a failed query), `null` when it was

UserAnalyticsUpdatedResponse.description: How many fired events of a user alert a call acknowledged

updated.description: The number of events that were acknowledged by the call
